sentences.en: Hey, I'm Benjamin Poulin.
sentences.zh: 嘿，我是本杰明·普兰。

sentences.en: And I'm Mark Ronson.
sentences.zh: 我是马克·朗森。

sentences.en: And welcome to The Reframers, a podcast that's all about the love of design and the culture that surrounds it.
sentences.zh: 欢迎收听《重构者》，这是一档专注于设计之美及其周边文化的播客。

sentences.en: Even back when I was DJing in nightclubs in the era of vinyl, every night you took 300 of your most prized possessions to work with you, and you turned a DJ booth
sentences.zh: 即使是在黑胶唱片时代的夜店做DJ时，你每晚都要带着300件你最珍视的宝贝去工作，然后你把DJ台

sentences.en: into this, like, living pop-up museum of beautiful 50-year-old artifacts.
sentences.zh: 变成了一个活生生的、展示着精美50年历史文物的快闪博物馆。

sentences.en: Listen to The Reframers from Audemars Piguet now on your favorite podcast platforMs.
sentences.zh: 现在就在你最喜欢的播客平台上收听爱彼出品的《重构者》吧。

sentences.en: From The New York Times, I'm Michael Barbaro.
sentences.zh: 我是《纽约时报》的迈克尔·巴尔巴罗。

sentences.en: This is The Daily.
sentences.zh: 这是《每日新闻》。

sentences.en: Today, Republicans delay a vote on their tax bill after a report that the economics were off by a trillion dollars.
sentences.zh: 今天，共和党人推迟了税改法案的投票，此前有报告称该法案的经济测算有万亿美元的误差。

sentences.en: And the White House's elaborate plan to replace the Secretary of State with the head of the CIA and replace the head of the CIA with a sitting senator.
sentences.zh: 还有白宫那项复杂的计划：用中情局局长取代国务卿，再由一位现任参议员接替中情局局长。

sentences.en: It's Friday, December 1St.
sentences.zh: 今天是12月1日，星期五。

sentences.en: So, Jim, throughout the day on Thursday, all the momentum seemed headed toward a vote on the Republican tax bill.
sentences.zh: 那么，吉姆，周四一整天，所有的势头似乎都指向共和党税改法案的投票。

sentences.en: Then what happened?
sentences.zh: 后来发生了什么？

sentences.en: Well, the official scorekeepers of Congress, the Joint Committee on Taxation, sort of dropped a bomb into the process.
sentences.zh: 嗯，国会的官方计分机构——国会税务联合委员会，在这一进程中投下了一枚“炸弹”。

sentences.en: Jim Tankersley covers taxes and the economy.
sentences.zh: 吉姆·坦克斯利负责报道税务和经济。

sentences.en: They released a long-awaited economic analysis of the tax bill that says, this is how much we think it's going to grow the economy, and this is how much tax revenue
sentences.zh: 他们发布了一份期待已久的税改法案经济分析报告，报告指出，我们认为这能带来多少经济增长，以及我们认为

sentences.en: we think it's going to produce.
sentences.zh: 它能产生多少税收收入。

sentences.en: And then you subtract that from the cost of the overall tax cuts, and you find, well, will this leave a big budget deficit at the end of 10 years?
sentences.zh: 然后你从整体减税的成本中减去这些收入，就会发现，嗯，这是否会在10年后留下巨大的预算赤字？

sentences.en: And what the committee said was, yeah, it's going to raise deficits by about a trillion dollars over 10 years, which is a big number, particularly for fiscal conservatives.
sentences.zh: 委员会的结论是，是的，它将在10年内增加约1万亿美元的赤字，这是一个巨大的数字，尤其是对财政保守派而言。

sentences.en: How much did Republicans anticipate that this bill might generate in terms of deficit?
sentences.zh: 共和党人预期这项法案会产生多少赤字？

sentences.en: So, Republicans have been coy about this, but they have generally said that they think the bill will pay for itself.
sentences.zh: 共和党人对此一直闪烁其词，但他们普遍表示，他们认为该法案可以实现收支平衡。

sentences.en: And there are $1.4 trillion in tax cuts in the Senate bill, which would mean zero extra deficits.
sentences.zh: 参议院法案中有1.4万亿美元的减税额，这意味着零额外赤字。

sentences.en: So they were off by a trillion, roughly speaking.
sentences.zh: 所以粗略来说，他们算错了1万亿。

sentences.en: I mean, how could people in Congress putting together a bill of this scale be off by such an extraordinarily large amount of money,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，国会里制定如此大规模法案的人，怎么会算错如此惊人的巨额资金，

sentences.en: $1 trillion?
sentences.zh: 整整1万亿美元？

sentences.en: Well, they say it's the committee that's off.
sentences.zh: 嗯，他们说是委员会算错了。

sentences.en: They say that the committee is just not seeing what they see in terms of how much growth will be created by tax cuts.
sentences.zh: 他们认为委员会只是没看到他们所看到的，即减税能带来多少增长。

sentences.en: Fundamentally, what this comes down to is,
sentences.zh: 从根本上说，问题的核心在于，

sentences.en: Republicans just are really true believers in the growth power of tax cuts, and they have talked themselves into the idea that these cuts will pay for themselves,
sentences.zh: 共和党人是减税增长效力的忠实信徒，他们已经说服自己相信这些减税措施能实现收支平衡，

sentences.en: even though no other credible model of this bill that we've seen has suggested they would come anywhere close.
sentences.zh: 尽管我们所见过的该法案的其他任何可靠模型都表明，它们根本达不到那种程度。

sentences.en: Okay, so members of Congress find out on Thursday night that their tax bill will blow a trillion-dollar hole in the deficit, according to this analysis.
sentences.zh: 好的，那么国会议员们在周四晚上发现，根据这份分析，他们的税改法案会在赤字上捅出一个万亿美元的窟窿。

sentences.en: How do they react?
sentences.zh: 他们作何反应？

sentences.en: Well, most of them kind of shrug it off.
sentences.zh: 嗯，他们大多数人对此不以为意。

sentences.en: But one very important Republican, Bob Corker, and another, Jeff Flake, seem to really take it seriously.
sentences.zh: 但有两位非常重要的共和党人，鲍勃·科克和杰夫·弗莱克，似乎真的认真对待了。

sentences.en: It stops them in their tracks.
sentences.zh: 这让他们停下了脚步。

sentences.en: It doubles down on their commitment to make sure the bill is fiscally responsible in their view.
sentences.zh: 这更加坚定了他们确保法案在他们看来符合财政责任的决心。

sentences.en: And so they are trying to find a mechanism by which to ensure that the bill will not lose a bunch of money and add to the debt, and so then the drama begins.
sentences.zh: 因此，他们试图寻找一种机制来确保该法案不会损失大量资金并增加债务，于是戏剧性的一幕开始了。

sentences.en: What we're seeing is something that was not expected by senior Republican aides, was not expected by Republican lawmakers walking into the vote.
sentences.zh: 我们所看到的是共和党高级助手们没预料到的，也是共和党议员们在进入投票时没预料到的。

sentences.en: Right now, there is a vote on the Senate floor.
sentences.zh: 现在，参议院正在进行投票。

sentences.en: It's largely a pro forma vote.
sentences.zh: 这在很大程度上是一次程序性投票。

sentences.en: It is a Democratic motion to send the tax plan back to committee.
sentences.zh: 这是一项由民主党提出的将税改计划退回委员会的动议。

sentences.en: Republicans have to go back to the drawing board to address the concerns of deficit hawks like Senator Bob Corker.
sentences.zh: 共和党人必须重新回到起草阶段，以解决像鲍勃·科克参议员这样的赤字鹰派人士的担忧。

sentences.en: So what do these two senators propose on Thursday as a solution to this trillion-dollar problem?
sentences.zh: 那么这两位参议员在周四提出了什么方案来解决这个万亿美元的问题？

sentences.en: So earlier in the week,
sentences.zh: 在本周早些时候，

sentences.en: Senator Corker had reached a deal with Republican leaders to allay some of his concerns on the deficit, and that deal was a trigger, what's called a trigger,
sentences.zh: 科克参议员与共和党领导人达成了一项协议，以缓解他的一些赤字担忧，该协议是一个触发机制，所谓的“触发器”，

sentences.en: where it would raise revenue by increasing taxes if tax revenues were not coming in to the degree to which Republicans had hoped they would.
sentences.zh: 如果税收收入没有达到共和党人预期的程度，它将通过增加税收来增加收入。

sentences.en: So essentially, if there were bigger deficits than they thought there'd be, it would force tax increases.
sentences.zh: 所以本质上，如果赤字比他们预想的要大，它就会强制加税。

sentences.en: So this is like a safety measure to protect against the deficits ballooning if this economic activity
sentences.zh: 所以这就像是一种安全措施，防止如果经济活动

sentences.en: doesn't create the promised revenue that would make up for the tax bill.
sentences.zh: 不能创造出足以弥补税改法案的预期收入，赤字就会膨胀。

sentences.en: Yeah, exactly.
sentences.zh: 是的，没错。

sentences.en: It was sort of an elegant solution.
sentences.zh: 这算是一个优雅的解决方案。

sentences.en: Not everybody liked it.
sentences.zh: 并不是每个人都喜欢它。

sentences.en: Controversial among Republicans and among wonks, but it was what they agreed to.
sentences.zh: 在共和党人和政策专家中存在争议，但这是他们同意的方案。

sentences.en: And then on Thursday, they hit a roadblock, which was that the Senate parliamentarian said, eh, you can't do this on the bill.
sentences.zh: 然后在周四，他们遇到了障碍，参议院议事规则专家说，呃，你们不能在法案中这样做。

sentences.en: We just got word from Republican leadership that the fiscal trigger is not allowed under the rules of the Senate.
sentences.zh: 我们刚刚从共和党领导层得到消息，根据参议院规则，财政触发器是不被允许的。

sentences.en: The idea of a fiscal trigger is now off the table because it does not comply with Senate rules.
sentences.zh: 财政触发器的想法现在被搁置了，因为它不符合参议院的规则。

sentences.en: There's this moment when it all comes on to the C-SPAN cameras, which are, I mean, the C-SPAN cameras are our new favorite soap opera nationally.
sentences.zh: 有那么一刻，这一切都呈现在C-SPAN的摄像机前，我的意思是，C-SPAN的摄像机现在是我们全国最喜欢的肥皂剧。

sentences.en: They were during our healthcare debate.
sentences.zh: 在我们的医改辩论期间是这样。

sentences.en: They are again here in the tax debate.
sentences.zh: 在这次税改辩论中也是如此。

sentences.en: And it's a particular type of soap opera called concerned senators standing around looking worried at each other.
sentences.zh: 这是一种特殊的肥皂剧，叫做“忧心忡忡的参议员们围在一起，看起来很担心对方”。

sentences.en: And what happened here was apparently the ruling had come down and there was a motion the Democrats had made to send the bill back to committee.
sentences.zh: 这里发生的事情显然是裁决已经下达，民主党人提出了一项动议，要求将法案退回委员会。

sentences.en: And Corker and Flake and then Ron Johnson of Wisconsin, a third Republican, had refused to vote down that motion.
sentences.zh: 而科克、弗莱克，还有威斯康星州的罗恩·约翰逊，第三位共和党人，拒绝否决该动议。

sentences.en: And so they stood for about an hour on the Senate floor in discussion with various states of agitated Republican leaders while they figured out what they were going to do
sentences.zh: 于是他们在参议院大厅里站了大约一个小时，与处于各种焦躁状态的共和党领导人进行讨论，同时他们想办法

sentences.en: to appease them just to the point of getting them to vote no on that motion so they could keep going with the bill.
sentences.zh: 安抚他们，直到让他们在动议中投下反对票，这样他们才能继续推进法案。

sentences.en: And then they could, you know, retire to, again, the back rooms and other parts of the Capitol off camera to try to figure out what they were going to do.
sentences.zh: 然后他们就可以，你知道，退回到国会大厦的密室和其他地方，避开镜头，试图弄清楚他们要做什么。

sentences.en: So in other words, these three Republicans are so troubled by this trillion dollar problem that they can't address with this trigger, that they're not going to block Democrats
sentences.zh: 换句话说，这三位共和党人对这个万亿美元的问题感到非常困扰，以至于他们无法用这个触发器来解决，他们不会阻止民主党人

sentences.en: from sending this entire bill back to committee, which would probably totally derail the thing.
sentences.zh: 将整个法案退回委员会，这可能会彻底破坏这件事。

sentences.en: And this has single-handedly held up a $1.4 trillion tax plan.
sentences.zh: 而这单枪匹马地阻碍了一项1.4万亿美元的税改计划。

sentences.en: This deficit concern is absolutely the thing that appears to be slowing the train down.
sentences.zh: 这种对赤字的担忧绝对是目前看起来正在拖慢火车速度的事情。

sentences.en: So what now?
sentences.zh: 那么现在怎么办？

sentences.en: What happens?
sentences.zh: 会发生什么？

sentences.en: So they're going to come back Friday morning.
sentences.zh: 他们周五早上会回来。

sentences.en: They're going to do some more voting on the floor on some more amendments.
sentences.zh: 他们会在大厅里对更多修正案进行投票。

sentences.en: But the big actions behind the scenes, they're going to try to craft a solution to appease Senators Corker and Flake.
sentences.zh: 但幕后的重大行动是，他们将试图制定一个解决方案来安抚科克和弗莱克参议员。

sentences.en: Now, it's important to note that they could theoretically pass this without them.
sentences.zh: 现在，需要注意的是，理论上他们可以在没有他们的情况下通过法案。

sentences.en: They can afford to lose two votes.
sentences.zh: 他们输得起两张票。

sentences.en: So if in the end they could get Senator Johnson and Senator Susan Collins and a couple of others who've been on the fence, I mean, they're very close.
sentences.zh: 所以如果最终他们能争取到约翰逊参议员、苏珊·柯林斯参议员和其他几个一直摇摆不定的人，我的意思是，他们非常接近了。

sentences.en: So they could theoretically get it through without those two guys.
sentences.zh: 所以理论上他们可以在没有那两个人的情况下通过它。

sentences.en: It just, that would be an outcome that a lot of people, I think, did not anticipate before this all started.
sentences.zh: 只是，那将是一个我认为很多人在这一切开始前没有预料到的结果。

sentences.en: And that would mean that at least 50 Republicans would vote for a bill that they know creates a trillion-dollar deficit in 10 years.
sentences.zh: 这意味着至少50名共和党人将投票支持一项他们知道会在10年内造成万亿美元赤字的法案。

sentences.en: That would mean that 50 Republicans would vote for a bill that they believe does not create that kind of deficit, but that congressional scorekeepers say would.
sentences.zh: 这意味着50名共和党人将投票支持一项他们认为不会造成那种赤字，但国会计分机构却说会造成赤字的法案。

sentences.en: Jim, what do you make of something like this?
sentences.zh: 吉姆，你对这样的事情怎么看？

sentences.en: The underlying economics of this bill being so called into question, the kind of foundation of the thing happening so close to the vote.
sentences.zh: 这项法案的基本经济学原理受到如此质疑，这种基础性的问题在投票前夕才出现。

sentences.en: What does it tell us?
sentences.zh: 这告诉了我们什么？

sentences.en: Well, it tells us a couple of things.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这告诉了我们几件事。

sentences.en: One, it tells us that this process has moved exceedingly fast and that you might expect something like this when the process is moving really faSt.
sentences.zh: 第一，这告诉我们这个过程推进得太快了，当过程推进得非常快时，你可能会预料到会发生这样的事情。

sentences.en: A speed bump, wow, when you hit the speed bump in the car when you're going 60, that's a big deal.
sentences.zh: 减速带，哇，当你以60英里的时速开车撞上减速带时，那可是件大事。

sentences.en: And that's what it kind of feels like right now.
sentences.zh: 这就是现在给人的感觉。

sentences.en: But I think the other thing is that for those of us who have covered economic policy for a long time, we have been hearing from Republicans over and over and over and over
sentences.zh: 但我认为另一件事是，对于我们这些长期报道经济政策的人来说，我们已经听共和党人反反复复说了

sentences.en: for the last eight, 10 years that debt was a primary, if not the primary hindrance to the economy booming the way that we want it to.
sentences.zh: 过去八到十年里，债务是阻碍经济按我们想要的方式繁荣的主要障碍，如果不是唯一障碍的话。

sentences.en: And so to see them now kind of brush away those concerns to just say, hey, we don't believe the scorekeeper that we have been trying for years to get to do this kind of analysis
sentences.zh: 所以现在看到他们以这种方式扫除这些担忧，只是说，嘿，我们不相信我们多年来一直试图让其进行这种分析的计分机构，

sentences.en: now that they've done it we don't believe them.
sentences.zh: 现在他们做了分析，我们却不相信他们。

sentences.en: I think that's jarring.
sentences.zh: 我认为这令人震惊。

sentences.en: And it really does come down to
sentences.zh: 这确实归结为

sentences.en: Republicans are professing a much stronger faith in the ability for tax cuts to pay for themselves than we've seen in a long time, particularly since the tax cuts of the Bush era
sentences.zh: 共和党人对减税能实现收支平衡的能力表现出了比我们很长一段时间以来所见过的更强烈的信念，特别是考虑到布什时代的减税政策

sentences.en: did not pay for themselves.
sentences.zh: 并没有实现收支平衡。

sentences.en: It's sort of a faith in conservative economic philosophy more than anything else.
sentences.zh: 这与其说是一种经济分析，不如说是一种对保守派经济哲学的信仰。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: You know, years ago, a couple years ago, I did a profile of Arthur Laffer, the conservative economist who sort of pioneered this idea.
sentences.zh: 你知道，几年前，我为阿瑟·拉弗做过一个人物专访，他是那种开创了这一理念的保守派经济学家。

sentences.en: And he was espousing this faith, and it was before the 2016 election, and he was telling me how much every Republican candidate was coming to him to talk about this.
sentences.zh: 他当时正在宣扬这种信仰，那是在2016年大选之前，他告诉我每一位共和党候选人是如何来找他谈论这个问题的。

sentences.en: And he was sort of like doing a revival of it.
sentences.zh: 他当时就像是在进行一场复兴运动。

sentences.en: And I think we're seeing that right now.
sentences.zh: 我认为我们现在正看到这一点。

sentences.en: We're seeing a revival of this thinking and the belief that we really are held back by high taxes and that if we just cut them, we really will have extraordinary growth
sentences.zh: 我们正在看到这种思想的复兴，以及一种信念，即我们确实被高税收所束缚，如果我们削减税收，我们确实会再次拥有非凡的增长

sentences.en: in America again, and everything will work out.
sentences.zh: 在美国，一切都会好起来的。

sentences.en: Jim, thank you.
sentences.zh: 吉姆，谢谢你。

sentences.en: You're welcome.
sentences.zh: 不客气。

sentences.en: On Thursday evening,
sentences.zh: 周四晚上，

sentences.en: Senate Majority Leader Mitch McConnell said lawmakers would reconvene at 11 a.m.
sentences.zh: 参议院多数党领袖米奇·麦康奈尔表示，议员们将于上午11点重新开会，

sentences.en: to begin voting on amendments before a final vote on the bill later today.
sentences.zh: 在今天晚些时候对法案进行最终投票前，开始对修正案进行投票。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: Hi, I'm Andrew Ross-Sorkin.
sentences.zh: 嗨，我是安德鲁·罗斯-索金。

sentences.en: I cover business and policy for DealBook, a daily newsletter at The New York Times.
sentences.zh: 我为《纽约时报》的每日通讯《DealBook》报道商业和政策。

sentences.en: On November 18th,
I'm going to be interviewing some of the most consequential leaders in business, politics, and culture, including J.D.
sentences.zh: 我将在纽约市举行的DealBook峰会上现场采访一些商业、政治和文化领域最有影响力的领导人，包括J.D.

sentences.en: Vance,
sentences.zh: 万斯、

sentences.en: Elon Musk, Christine Lagarde,
sentences.zh: 埃隆·马斯克、克里斯蒂娜·拉加德、

sentences.en: Zilran Mondani, and many others live on stage at the DealBook Summit in New York City.
sentences.zh: 齐尔兰·蒙达尼以及其他许多人。

sentences.en: You can watch some of these unguarded, unfiltered conversations as they happen.
sentences.zh: 你可以观看其中一些毫无防备、未经剪辑的对话。

sentences.en: We're going to be live streaming select interviews for anyone to watch free at nytimes.com on November 18th.
sentences.zh: 我们将于11月18日在nytimes.com上直播部分采访，供所有人免费观看。
